title: FILL: short title, e.g. Security review of example-tool 1.2.3

review.reviewer: FILL: who ran it, e.g. Codex with NoBrainer.Tech Flow

target.kind: FILL: repository | skill | installer | package | fixture | other
target.label: FILL: name of the reviewed tool
target.location: FILL: URL, package id or local path
target.ref: FILL: exact commit SHA or version; use null for a local folder without Git
target.ref_note: FILL: how the target was pinned, e.g. local folder, sha256 of its files in digest; or delete this line
target.digest: FILL: artifact digest, or delete this line
target.local_modifications: FILL: dirty paths of a local checkout, or None

authority.data_classification: FILL: e.g. Public source; no private data was read
authority.write_execution: FILL: e.g. Read-only static inspection; nothing was installed or run

scope.headline: FILL: one line, e.g. Six files reviewed. Everything else out of scope.

reviewed.path: FILL: relative path that you read
reviewed.note: FILL: short note, or delete this line

excluded: FILL: what you did not review and why
scope.boundary: FILL: the named paths only; no whole-disk, whole-home or whole-system scan

network.note: FILL: e.g. Registry metadata and archive read into memory

decision_brief.lede: FILL: two or three plain sentences a non-expert can act on
summary: FILL: what you found, in plain words
result_meaning: FILL: what this result means and does not mean

surface_review.summary: FILL: README, skill, prompt and installer text
FILL: access to secrets, keys, browser or home files
FILL: direct, encoded or indirect outbound data
FILL: AI agent tools, MCP, hooks and CI permissions
FILL: installers, lifecycle scripts and downloads
FILL: manifests, lockfiles, sources and integrity

findings.title: FILL: short finding title
findings.severity: FILL: High | Critical | Medium | Low | Informational
findings.surface: FILL: installer_lifecycle | egress | credential_personal_files | social_engineering | agent_tools_hooks_ci | dependencies
findings.trace: FILL: trigger, reachable code, data and destination
findings.trigger: FILL: what starts it, e.g. npm install runs preinstall
findings.existing_control: FILL: the guard that exists, or None
findings.impact: FILL: what could happen to the user
findings.evidence_summary: FILL: what the evidence proves and what it does not

evidence.label: FILL: short label
evidence.excerpt: FILL: a few lines, secrets removed

findings.required_verification: FILL: how to verify the fix without running untrusted code

rejected_candidates.title: FILL: suspicious-looking item that is not a finding
rejected_candidates.reason: FILL: why it is not a finding

dependency_age.status: FILL: NEEDS_SETUP | NOT_APPLICABLE | CONFIGURATION_OBSERVED | ENFORCEMENT_VERIFIED | UNSUPPORTED | NOT_ASSESSED
summary: FILL: status of the 14-day rule in plain words, with its limits

assessments.package_manager: FILL: npm, pnpm, pip or other
assessments.config_source: FILL: e.g. No .npmrc in the repository
assessments.scope: FILL: project, user, CI or registry
assessments.status: FILL: NEEDS_SETUP | NOT_APPLICABLE | CONFIGURATION_OBSERVED | ENFORCEMENT_VERIFIED | UNSUPPORTED | NOT_ASSESSED
assessments.window: FILL: e.g. None found; recommended min-release-age=14
assessments.limits: FILL: what this setting would not cover

checks_run: FILL: each check you actually ran, e.g. python3 tools/inspect_package.py npm:left-pad@1.3.0
limits: FILL: what this review could not see or prove
owner_gates: FILL: decisions only the owner can make, e.g. approve a fix or an isolated test

next_steps.title: FILL: next step
next_steps.text: FILL: what to do and why
